$comment: Application-fit rules taken from published Axim and Corvus specifications.
WHY EVERY ROW CARRIES A SOURCE
Earlier in this project I concluded from site navigation that the Corvus 6420
did not exist and edited a rule accordingly. It does exist. So the rule for
this file is that no figure appears here unless it is printed on a datasheet,
and the row names the document and the line it came from. A reviewer must be
able to check any number in under a minute.
Anything I could not source is not here. Inventing thresholds for equipment
that quotes real money is the one thing this tool must not do.
THE PORTFOLIO IS A SOURCE, NOT A BROCHURE
TTO and VIJ were empty for a while on the grounds that Axim publishes no
datasheet PDF for them. That was wrong. The captured product pages carry
specification tables — the T400 pages give the thermal bar size, the ambient
range and an IP rating, and the IV pages give print speeds, print distance
and print height. It was all sitting in the captured pages while the
two technologies had no rules at all.
IP20 on the T400 and XL series is the most valuable line in any of it. The
second digit of an IP rating is water and 0 means none, so a washdown line
rules the technology out rather than derating it.
The same was true of TIJ, whose figures are on the TJ500 and TJ1000 pages.
Its 50°F floor is the highest in the range — every other technology here is
rated to 40 or 41°F — so a cool room that suits a CIJ can be out of spec for
a thermal jet, and nothing would have said so.
What the portfolio does not carry is the engineering judgement on the
application analysis form: air turbulence, guide rails, washdown. Those are
quoted verbatim into data/application-analysis-notes.md and cited from there,
so a reviewer can check every word against something in the repository.

VIJ    data/sources/pages/iv18-dot-...md, iv9-dot-...md

UNIT CONVERSIONS ARE SHOWN, NOT HIDDEN
The datasheets state character height in inches and the profile holds
millimetres. Each row shows the inch figure it came from alongside the
millimetre threshold, so a conversion error is visible rather than buried.

rules.author: Axim PL6300 datasheet

actions.message: Past the fastest stated PL6300 figure of 300 fpm. Refer to Application Engineering.

rules.author: Axim PL6300 datasheet

rules.author: Axim ScanMark spec sheet

rules.summary: Above 250 fpm the Ridgeline 3200 is past its fastest published figure.
rules.detail: Ridgeline 3200 technical data, Print speed: 'Alphanumeric text: Up to 250 FPM @ 200 DPI'. That is the fastest number on the sheet, and it already assumes 200 DPI rather than the 300 DPI the head can reach.
rules.author: Axim Ridgeline 3200 datasheet

actions.message: Past the fastest published Ridgeline figure of 250 fpm at 200 DPI. Refer to Application Engineering.

rules.summary: Holding 300 DPI on the Ridgeline 3200 costs line speed.
rules.detail: Ridgeline 3200 technical data, Print speed: 'Up to 250 FPM @ 200 DPI' and 'Up to 130 FPM @ 300 DPI', with the note 'Higher line speeds achievable with reduction of DPI'. Above 130 fpm the resolution has to come down, so quote the resolution the line speed allows rather than the best the head can do.
rules.author: Axim Ridgeline 3200 datasheet

actions.message: 300 DPI is published to 130 fpm. Above that the resolution drops toward 200 DPI — confirm which the code needs.

rules.summary: Barcodes on the Ridgeline 3200 are published to 150 fpm.
rules.detail: Ridgeline 3200 technical data, Print speed: 'Barcode: Up to 150 FPM @ 200 DPI'. Barcode work has its own, lower figure than text, and a scannable code is the whole point of quoting the machine.
rules.author: Axim Ridgeline 3200 datasheet

actions.message: Barcode print is published to 150 fpm at 200 DPI. This line is faster — get the code verified before quoting.

rules.author: Axim Ridgeline 3200 datasheet

actions.message: Published throw is up to 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) for text, and application dependent. This gap is wider.

rules.author: Axim Ridgeline 3200 datasheet

rules.summary: Thermal transfer overprinters are rated IP20 — no liquid protection at all.
rules.detail: T406/6e, T408/8e and the Thorne T800 all publish 'IP Rate: IP20'. The second digit of an IP rating is water, and 0 means no protection whatsoever. This is not a machine to derate for a washdown line; it is a machine to keep out of one, or to enclose.
rules.author: Axim T400 and T800 product pages

actions.message: Published IP20 — no water protection. A washdown line needs an enclosure quoted, or a different technology.

rules.summary: The T400 series is rated 41-104°F.
rules.detail: T402+ and T404+ specifications: 'Environmental Temperature 5 - 40°C (41-104°F)'. T406/6e, T408/8e and the T800 publish the same 5-40°C range. Cited to the spec sheet rather than the product page from 8 August 2026: the figure is stated in both and a spec sheet is the stronger reference.

actions.message: Rated to 104°F. This area runs hotter — the position or the cooling needs reviewing.

rules.author: Axim T400 product pages

Cited to the spec sheet rather than the product page from 8 August 2026: the figure is stated in both and a spec sheet is the stronger reference.

The hierarchy files all of these under one Product Type of 'T400 Series', so a rule cannot tell which is on the quote — hence a caveat naming the machine that takes the next step, rather than a refusal.
rules.author: Thorne T400 spec sheet

actions.message: Taller than the largest print area any Thorne T400 document states, 213 mm on the T408. Refer to Application Engineering.

rules.summary: A print wider than 80 mm puts the XL Series into continuous mode.
rules.detail: The sheet gives two print areas, and they are not close: 53 x 80 mm intermittent against 53 x 300 mm continuous. Width is the whole difference — the height is 53 mm either way — so a message wider than 80 mm is not a machine problem, it is a mode decision, and it costs throughput. See A-TTO-XL-RATE-CM: continuous is published at 250 prints a minute against 450 intermittent. A rep who has quoted 400 a minute AND a 200 mm wide message has quoted something the sheet does not offer.
rules.sourceRef: Datasheets/Literature_TTO_ThorneT800_SpecSheetWEB.md, Print Area (HxW) Intermittent — '53 x 80 mm (2.1 x 3.1 inches)'
rules.author: Thorne T800 spec sheet

actions.message: Wider than the 80 mm intermittent print area. The XL Series reaches 300 mm in continuous mode, which is published at 250 prints a minute rather than 450.

rules.summary: 300 mm is the widest print the XL Series publishes.
rules.detail: 53 x 300 mm in continuous mode is the larger of the two print areas on the sheet, and there is no third. A caveat rather than a refusal for the same reason A-TTO-BAR-53 is: the hierarchy files the whole Thorne range under one product type, so this cannot tell one XL variant from another.
rules.sourceRef: Datasheets/Literature_TTO_ThorneT800_SpecSheetWEB.md, Print Area (HxW) Continuous — '53 x 300 mm (2.1 x 11.8 inches)'
rules.author: Thorne T800 spec sheet

actions.message: Wider than the 300 mm continuous print area, which is the largest the XL Series publishes.

rules.summary: Above 250 a minute the XL Series has to run intermittently.
rules.detail: Two performance figures at 5 mm print height: 450 prints per minute intermittent, 250 continuous. A-TTO-XL-RATE already refuses above 450; this is the line below it, where the rate is still available but only in the mode that caps the print at 80 mm wide. Both figures are stated against their own label on the sheet, which is why they can be quoted.
rules.sourceRef: Datasheets/Literature_TTO_ThorneT800_SpecSheetWEB.md, Performance CM at 5mm Print Height — '250 Prints Per Minute'
rules.author: Thorne T800 spec sheet

actions.message: Above the 250 a minute continuous figure. This rate needs intermittent mode, where the print area is 80 mm wide rather than 300.

rules.summary: The published apply rate depends on the product spacing.
rules.detail:
The sheet states the rate and then states what it depends on, in the same row: 'Single Apply: Up to 52 PPM; Dual Apply: Up to 28 PPM' followed by 'Dependent on Label Length, Print Speed and Product Spacing'. So 52 a minute is a ceiling under conditions, not a number to quote against a line whose spacing nobody has checked.

No minimum spacing is published anywhere, which is why this states the dependency instead of grading it. Writing a threshold here would mean inventing one. It fires only when the rep has answered the spacing question and is asking for more than the dual-apply figure — the point at which the three variables start trading against each other.
rules.sourceRef: Datasheets/Axim PL6300 All-Electric Print and Apply Labeler Datasheet 4P.md, Product Rate — 'Dependent on Label Length, Print Speed and Product Spacing'
rules.author: Axim PL6300 datasheet

actions.message: The published apply rate is stated as dependent on label length, print speed and product spacing. Confirm the rate holds at this line's spacing before quoting it.

rules.summary: The valve jet prints 9 dots across; a logo needs a hundred times that.
rules.detail: IV9 specifications: 'Print resolution 9 x 25 DPI'. IV18: '8 x 25 DPI'. Nine dots across the web is a character built from a dot matrix you can count, which is what a valve jet is for — a large, cheap, robust mark on a case. It is not a printing process a logo or a retail-quality code can be asked of, and the difference from a thermal jet's 300 x 300 is not a matter of degree.
rules.author: Axim IV series product page

actions.message: The valve jet resolves 9 dots across the web. For a graded code or a logo this is the wrong process — a thermal jet or the high-resolution inkjet is.

rules.summary: A scannable barcode off a valve jet needs proving before it is quoted.
rules.detail: IV9 specifications: 'Print resolution 9 x 25 DPI'. A linear barcode can be built from a coarse matrix and often scans; whether THIS one does depends on the symbology, the X dimension and the substrate, and none of those is a figure the datasheet settles. Stated as a caveat rather than a refusal because valve jets do print scannable codes in the field — and rather than silence, because the machine beside it in the list resolves thirty times finer for the same answer.
rules.author: Axim IV series product page

actions.message: 9 x 25 DPI. Linear codes can scan off a valve jet, but prove it on the customer's substrate before quoting it.

rules.summary: 300 x 300 DPI is what a graded code or a logo needs.
rules.detail: HP 0.5" and HP 1.0" specifications: 'Print resolution 300 x 300 DPI'. This is the answer to the question the valve jet is refused for, and saying so positively is the point — a rep who has just been told the valve jet will not do it should be able to see what will.
rules.author: Axim thermal jet product page

actions.message: 300 x 300 DPI, which covers a graded barcode or a logo.

rules.summary: Holding 300 DPI costs the thermal jet its top speed.
rules.detail: HP 0.5" specifications: 'Print resolution 300 x 300 DPI' and 'Print speeds w/ reduced resolution Up to 500 FPM'. The 500 figure is the REDUCED-resolution one, so a line running near it is not also getting 300 DPI. Which of the two gives way is a decision for the customer, and it can only be put to them if somebody knows the code has to be graded.
rules.author: Axim thermal jet product page

actions.message: The 500 fpm figure is at REDUCED resolution. Above 200 fpm, check the customer will accept the print this gives at speed.
